title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — Christ-words for a creature? Calvin & Augustine forbid
pass_a_gloss: GAR presses Calvin and Augustine: those words claim unique divine power for Christ alone. Would Augustine ever let them fit a creature, in jest or in earnest? Acknowledge the Creator; discern the creature. Hold the force of that reply. Hold the force of that reply.
pass_b_english: GAR. And there can be some reason why someone should apply to an infant or to any man whatever those words by which, Calvin testifying, Christ exempts himself from the common crowd of men, and claims for himself alone the divine power, whose sense from the beginning of the world has been diffused through all ages. Do you think holy Augustine would have suffered this place to be accommodated to a creature, whether in jest or in earnest—he who, when he had diligently meditated those words, exclaims, Acknowledge the Creator, discern the creature?
source_text: GAR. Et quaedam ratio esse potest, ut quis ad infantem vel hominem quemcumque applicet ea verba, quibus teste Calvino Christus eximit se a vulgo hominum, sibiique solius divinam virtutem vindicat, cuius sensus ab initio usque mundi in omnia saecula diffusus fuerit. Putasne passurum Sanctum Augustinum, ut hic locus vel ioco, vel serio ad creaturam accommodaretur, qui cum ea verba diligenter meditatus esset, exclamat, Agnoscite Creatorem, discernite creaturam?

choices.choice: Calvin/Augustine: Christ-words not for any creature
